Almost 13 years later, I finally played this game—and my only regret is not playing it sooner! Batman: Arkham City GOTY was an incredible experience, a true gem among superhero open-world action games. I had high expectations going in, and to my surprise, the game not only met but exceeded them (aside from a few small annoyances).

Story & Characters – A Masterclass in Superhero Narrative
The story is phenomenal, with Batman trying to save Arkham City from major threats like Hugo Strange and, most notably, Joker, who easily takes the crown as the best antagonist in the entire Arkham series. Mark Hamill delivers an outstanding performance as the Clown Prince of Crime, making every second of his voice acting an absolute treat. Joker constantly keeps the player on edge with his unpredictable nature, and his dynamic with Harley Quinn makes for an even greater threat to Gotham.

A quick side note: Harley Quinn’s Revenge DLC is a must-play. It perfectly captures Harley’s character as seen in Arkham Asylum, something that was unfortunately lost in Arkham Knight, Origins, and the disastrous Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League, where she was reduced to being loud, annoying, and dumb just for the sake of being dumb.

Heroes & Their Roles
Batman is portrayed exceptionally well. Several moments force him to make tough choices—saving multiple lives at the cost of one, particularly in situations involving Talia and Joker. I do wish Alfred had a bigger role, but I still appreciated his presence, guiding Bruce and helping him navigate the moral dilemmas and stopping Protocol 10.

Kevin Conroy delivers an outstanding performance, with some truly great lines, and his brilliance especially shines during Batman’s face-off with Penguin and Joker. In my opinion, he is the only true Batman, and his iconic voice will be deeply missed. Rest easy, legend.

Robin’s cameo felt underwhelming, and I really wish he had been a playable character instead of Catwoman, who, while a great character, took up more spotlight than necessary. That said, I didn’t mind her missions being interwoven with Batman’s story since they created suspenseful cliffhangers, making me even more eager to see what happened next. My only complaint is that her final mission takes place after the game’s ending credits, at a point where I no longer cared as much about her story an plot that was mostly finished. It felt forced and sluggish to complete. Also, her climbing mechanics are frustrating and extremely unsatisfying.

Gameplay & Atmosphere
The combat system is greatly improved, adding much more depth to fights. Enemies now have new weapons, shields, and minibosses wielding hammers and other heavy weapons. Titans also make a return, and they are incredibly satisfying to defeat. These additions make battles feel more dynamic and force players to think more strategically rather than just button-mashing through encounters.

The ending is pure cinema. The soundtrack throughout the entire game is phenomenal, but it really hits hard at the conclusion. Without spoiling anything, I was left in an abyss of thought, wondering: What’s next for Batman? I wanted to see more, to understand what was going through Bruce’s mind at that moment. The depth and foreshadowing in this game are incredible.

The only thing that felt slightly lacking compared to Arkham Asylum was the atmosphere. While Arkham City is a fantastic open world, it didn’t quite capture the same eerie, claustrophobic tension that made the first game so special (not like it had to).

Minor Issues & Logical Gaps
One of the strangest moments was the Mr. Freeze boss fight. While it was mechanically creative, it felt somewhat forced, as if the game just needed to include a boss battle. Story-wise, it didn’t make much sense—Batman would have helped Freeze’s wife regardless, given everything that had happened before (rescuing Freeze’s suit, saving him from Penguin, etc.).

Another oddity was the Hush side mission (Identity Thief). Somehow, Hush manages to escape Arkham City by trapping Batman in an apartment for, like, a minute. I refuse to believe that the same Batman who stops an entire city’s crime in one night just casually lets Hush walk free after a 60-second inconvenience. He even says, “I’ll hunt him down tomorrow,” yet it takes him nine months (canonically) to catch him in another game. 😂

Final Thoughts – Should You Play It?
Despite these minor flaws, I absolutely loved playing Arkham City, and it’s a game I will always appreciate and recommend—to you, the reader, and to anyone who enjoys superhero games and action-packed combat.

For me, Arkham Asylum is still my favorite due to its unforgettable atmosphere and the fact that it was my first Batman game. However, don’t let that stop you from playing this one—Arkham City is a massive, innovative upgrade over the first game and remains one of the best superhero stories ever told in gaming.

Buy it on sale if you can, but even at full price, it’s worth every penny for the sheer amount of content you get.

As the sequel to the amazing Arkham Asylum, City had a lot to live up to. Fortunately, it's not only on par with the original, but in many ways surpasses it. With NG+, more collectibles, more sidequests, and plenty more iconic enemies to beat down, this game really has it all. Most importantly, the combat is still response as ever, and they barely changed anything, only adding new gadgets to Batman's arsenal. After all, "If it ain't broke don't fix it," and Asylum's combat was anything but. Plus, the story is incredible, and even though it goes entirely off the rails for a while, it never stops being a fun ride. The entire climax feels like multiple mind-blowing twists in a row, and they do not disappoint.

I think the only criticism I have of this game are the Riddler sidequests, which involve the most blatantly obvious riddles ever riddled. Example, "I am a window you can't see through, but you can see you! This answer may require some REFLECTION." It will challenge your mental prowess only by bludgeoning it with simplicity. It will play games with your head, making you think its too easy, they must be setting up for a trick question, the answer to this one CAN'T be my own shadow, it's too obvious! You're wrong. Shouldn't second-guess yourself, Batman.

[h2][b]Arkham City > Arkham Knight[/b][/h2]

Even after all these years, Batman: Arkham City still feels like the moment superhero games figured out what they were supposed to be. It took the already solid foundation of Arkham Asylum and just expanded everything. Bigger world, better combat, more villains, and a story that actually feels like a full Batman graphic novel instead of just a game campaign.

I love that Arkham City's world is very small and compact, but very (content) dense, that to me is the best open world/level design. I hate vast, almost empty, no-level design open worlds that take forever to traverse and quests/missions/the story makes you go from one side of the giant map to the other. Instead of one location, you’re gliding across a quarantined chunk of Gotham controlled by different villains. [b]Joker, Penguin, Two-Face,[/b] and others all have their own territory, and it gives the city a chaotic “anything can happen” vibe. Side missions pop up constantly, letting you deal with smaller villains and making the world feel packed with Batman lore.

The stealth sections are just as good. There are way more tools and takedowns, and enemies are smarter with things like jammers and mines. Dropping into a room full of armed thugs, silently picking them off from gargoyles one by one, never gets old.

The story is another big highlight. Instead of every villain teaming up, they’re all working against each other while Batman tries to survive in the middle of it. Joker’s storyline especially stands out, and the ending is still one of the most memorable moments in any superhero game.

And the bosses. After Arkham Asylum’s weak boss fights, Arkham City completely fixes that. The Mr. Freeze fight alone is legendary because you have to use different stealth tactics every time or he adapts. It’s one of the most creative boss fights in gaming.

Even today, the game still holds up incredibly well. The combat is addictive, the soundtrack is epic, and the atmosphere of Arkham City makes Gotham feel alive in a way very few games manage.

[h1]READ THIS BEFORE LAUNCHING THE GAME[/h1]

During the installation process, along with the DirectX libraries another program will be installed called [b]AMD Dual-Core Optimizer[/b], which was meant to improve the performance on systems that run Windows XP and use old AMD Dual-Core CPUs.

On PCs that run Windows Vista and later and/or an Intel CPU, you won't need that program because it will impact the performance and cause other issues.

Unfortunately when you launch the game for the first time you don't get the choice to decline the installation of AMD Dual-Core Optimizer (that's why I left a negative review).
In order to stop that program from being installed, do as follows:

[i]If the program is already installed, you should uninstall it. Go to "Programs and Features", select "AMD Dual-Core Optimizer" and click "Uninstall" (perhaps it's going to take a while, do not cancel the process and wait for it to finish); afterwords, reboot the PC.[/i]

    1) Go to the installation folder of the game (right click on the game title -> properties -> local files tab -> browse local files)
    2) Open "installscript.vdf" (right click -> open with -> use Notepad)
    3) Scroll down until you see the word "AMD", followed by a bunch of code between the two perpendicular { and } brackets; delete that portion of code, beginning from the word "AMD" to the last perpendicular bracket (note that you must leave the brackets on the left side and everything else)
    4) Save the file. Make sure you didn't delete anything that has to do with DXSetup, VCRedist_x86 and DotNetFx35
    5) When you're done, go to the "Setup" folder and delete "amd_dc_opt.exe" (this is an optional step, just to be safe)

If you've done everything correctly, when you launch the game the installation of AMD Dual-Core Optimizer won't start.

[h1]Batman: Arkham City – A Love Letter to the Dark Knight[/h1]
[b]There’s a very specific kind of nostalgia that hits me when I think about Batman: Arkham City. It takes me right back to those humid afternoons after school, rushing over to my friend's house, dropping my bag, and fighting over the keyboard like it was the most important mission on Earth. We weren't just playing a game, we were living in Gotham. We were the Batman. And even now, years later, booting it up feels like coming home to a city that is, quite frankly, a beautiful, neon-soaked disaster.[/b]

[h1]The Ultimate Power Fantasy[/h1]
[b]Let’s get one thing straight, Arkham City didn't just set the bar for superhero games, it practically built the stadium. The "FreeFlow" combat system is still the gold standard. There is a primal, rhythmic satisfaction to it, a ballet of knuckle-sandwiches and cape-stuns. When you’re in the middle of a brawl, timing a counter-attack perfectly while a goon is swinging a lead pipe at your head, you feel like a ultimate powerhouse.
And then there’s the traversal. Gliding off the top of the GCR Tower, hearing the wind rush past you, and diving into a perfect grapple boost? It’s addictive. It’s the kind of movement that makes you forget about the objective entirely because you're having too much fun just existing in the space. It’s a city designed for a predator, and you are the apex.[/b]

[h1]A Gotham That Breathes (and Screams)[/h1]
[b]The atmosphere in this game is thick enough to cut with a Batarang. Transforming a massive chunk of Gotham into an open-air prison for the city's worst villains was a stroke of genius. The contrast between the cold, industrial decay and the garish, chaotic "decorations" of the Joker’s goons gives the world so much personality.
And the characters! Mark Hamill’s Joker isn't just a performance, it’s a terrifying, hilarious force of nature. Every time he crackles over the radio to mock you, you don't just want to finish the mission, you want to find him and make him stop talking. The story is high-stakes, deeply personal, and surprisingly tragic. It treats the source material with the kind of reverence that makes you feel like you’re playing through the greatest graphic novel ever written.[/b]

[i]Batman: Arkham City[/i] is an action-adventure game developed by Rocksteady Studios and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment.

[b]Story[/b]
I suggest playing through Arkham Asylum first, as events from that game are used as a setup to setting of this one.

Arkham City takes place 18 months after Arkham Asylum events. Taking credit for stopping Joker's siege, director Sharp becomes a Mayor of Gotham City. Declaring Asylum no longer suitable, he creates immense prison enclosure known as Arkham City inside Gotham's slums, taken care of by mysterious Hugo Strange while monitored by private military firm TYGER Security. Our protagonist, Bruce Wayne, opposes that idea and ends up in a titular prison himself. Here as Batman he wants to find out more about mysterious Protocol 10 and real intentions behind the prison.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
If you played Arkham Asylum, you already know what to expect as City builds up upon gameplay from previous game, providing third person open world venture where you will investigate, explore, stealth and brawl through the prison as our favourite Caped Crusader, searching for truth (and few faces to soak your fists in).
First thing you will experience is the main dish of the game- combat. Punch, kick, smack thugs before they smack you to avoid a dreadful fate of watching villians laugh in your face as you lose and reload a checkpoint. Counter or dodge incoming attacks, chain up combinations to gain speed and power, utilize plenty of gadgets to surprise your opponents. Game provides improved version of the "Freeflow" combat system, meaning you can now perform more moves, such as option to counter multiple attacks at once or being able to chain combinations for long enough to unleash deadly special attacks. Enemies can be armed with different armor and weapons, forcing you to adjust your moves accordingly.

Sometimes you get a chance to resolve encounters silently. Similar scenario as with first game, utilize vantage points, environment, detective vision and your gadgets to eliminate enemies without them noticing you. Watch as fear strikes their minds and heartpulse keeps rising with each performed takedown on their buddies, but just like in combat, thugs are a bit more Bat-proof this time so they come with more firearms, jammers and extra tools that will make your life harder, as tides can quickly shift back and forth. Know when to strike and when to wait for opportunity, or just create your own!

Arkham City opens up the area, providing way more space to explore. Glide, grapple and sprint around looking for collectibles that expand the narrative and lore, side activities, or just seek out local thugs waiting for a fight! (Or to be knocked out silently by a sneaky Bat.) Fans favourite Riddler returns with his trophies and riddles, while other villians make an appearance in side quests spread all over the prison, unlockable as you progress through the story. Same applies to gadgets, so you might have to wait a bit to obtain a tool or two before you can enter certain buildings or collect specific trophies. No pressure, you can always return to every area you visited.

Combat and exploration grant you experience points, earn enough to level Batman up and unlock new skills, moves, or improve gadgets.

[b]Playtime, other modes[/b]
It took me roughly 13 hours to complete everything in Arkham City. After beating the story you unlock New Game Plus where you can utilize everything you have unlocked with increased overall difficulty to balance it out. Additionally there is "Riddler's Revenge" mode, where you tackle on different challenge maps and campaigns for medals! Fair to say you can spend a bit more time in City than you might think at first glance, if interested. Especially as this version comes with extra DLC, Catwoman content, and extra characters in RR mode.

[b]Impressions[/b]
Out of the gate I will go out with a very bold claim- Arkham City is probably the best sequel I ever had a pleasure to play. A textbook definition of how they should be made. It's not a revolution, but an evolution. If you played Asylum you feel right at home almost instantly as game keeps same great controls and fantastic core gameplay allowing you to quickly get into action, increasing and opening up the location where game takes place, addition of side quests and expanded lore make it feel like an entirely new experience. Already great combat is now reaching superb levels, it's smooth, it's intuitive, with very tight controls and top notch precision when it comes to inputs as if game knows which thug you want to hit before you even do. Some annoying moments from Asylum where Batman in the middle of combination would decide to punch ghosts are gone, combined with new moves and gadgets it practically makes you beg for as many enemies on screen as possible to go wild.

But game knows when to slow down, when to give you a stealth section to showcase pretty solid enemy AI, allowing you to fully lean into Batman's strategic side with various gadgets, careful planning and utilization of environment to his advantage. Quite frankly it's a shame that because game is no longer as linear as first title, plus complete change of area where game takes place so it's almost impossible to just give you a stealth section in the middle of the city, it doesn't actually have that many of those section. But when you get them, it's an absolute treat to play.

Asylum no doubt had it's own unique atmosphere, but City is no slouch in that department either. Prison filled with crime in the middle of gang wars, with secrets on top of secrets, the mash of destroyed slums with iconic locations, freedom you get to explore it and encounter many more and lesser known villians across short yet satisfying side quests, it hits right. Fortunately game never feels too long, it doesn't drag on, even if you decide to dive into the madness that is collecting those forsaken trophies.
Fantastic audiovisual side, strong art direction, top of the game performance from voice actors and animators, game even today looks fairly impressive. Forgot to even mention expanded extra side mode of the game in which you can spend plenty hours, if running around Arkham City gets boring for you.

If there something...mixed, I can say about this game, it would probably be about the story. In my book the main villian in this one was a bit..disappointing? Especially as he was pretty much a "main face" when it came to promoting the game. I expected a better conclusion of certain arcs and felt like it could have focus on just one story, instead of jumping around and trying to have two main storylines branching out and at least for me, that never really worked. So yeah, story is enjoyable but I would like it to go into a different direction.

Nonetheless, Arkham City is simply superb. Easy recommendation. Combat feels great, explorating feels enjoyable, still holds up visually and it's a treat for fans of DC/Batman.

[b]Final words and conclusion[/b]
Said it before, gonna say it again, GOTY Edition comes with everything released so you get all the fun stuff- alternative costumes, post-main game DLC and extra characters- in one pack!

Batman: Arkham City improves pretty much everything from first game while still focusing on core strenghts- fantastic combat, great audiovisuals and intriguing exploration. Buy it, play it, enjoy it.

[quote]Gotham’s darkest secrets are out in the open—and the Bat is the only thing standing between chaos and order.[/quote]

[b]Batman: Arkham City[/b] takes everything great about the original Arkham Asylum and cranks it up to eleven. The sprawling prison district is a playground of shadows, danger, and detective work, giving you freedom to explore Gotham’s underbelly like never before.

Playing as the Dark Knight means blending intense combat, stealth, and gadget mastery. This game is the perfect example of how to do a sequel, improving on everything asylum did which was already an amazing game.

Take everything about the first game, Arkham Asylum, improve and expand upon it, then throw it on a much larger map and give you more "open world" things to do between story missions. That sums up Arkham City nicely. Sadly this also applies to the Riddler's trophies/riddles being incredibly frustrating and the number of "challenge" maps being called "content" expanding. With the GOTY edition you gain access to some nice alternate skins for the various characters on those challenge maps, and with a code you can alter Batman in the campaign(or during new game+). The other interesting new feature is the interweaving of a small Catwoman plot along Batman's journey, wich can provide the game with an alternate ending. Once the story is over the map goes completely open world, allowing you to finish off challenges and hunt down riddles as well as side quests. This part of the game also allows you to swap between Catwoman and Batman at 3 designated points, which saves your game, giving you a little control over where/when you can save. As a follow up, the GOTY edition also brings a short Harley based arc where you play as Robin for much of it. While short, this DLC adds a nice extra touch and some new things to do.

The only negative, really, is that there are still no choices to be made during the plot. This still almost entirely kills the replay value of the game for those not interested in the "challenge" maps. This is somewhat mitigated by Rocksteady having given the player a number of side quests that are entirely optional, and you can choose weather to chase them or not, as well as what order to do them in. Still most people will likely do them all on their first playthrough, removing what little incentive there is for a replay. 

New Game+ allows you to go through the whole story again, choosing your Batman outfit, with all of your gadgets unlocked at the start, allowing for a bit more freedom in how you go through events.

Overall I'll give it an 8.5/10 like Asylum. It did everything right that the previous game did, and more of it, but broke very little new ground.

One portion of the map is the Restricted Zone, which you're forced to go around, giving the accessible map a curved shape. This gives the illusion that the map is larger, since you can't go in a straight line to get from Joker's hideout at one end to Penguin's hideout at the other. There's no fast travel, but since the map is relatively small and traversal is fast and fun, there's no need for it.

Combat feels methodical and fun, and you usually have several choices for how you're going to handle a crowd of enemies. Will you disassemble an enemy's gun so nobody else can use it, or electrocute him so he shoots wildly and scares the rest of the enemies? Will you yank a distant enemy with the grappling gun to bring him closer, or knock him down with a batarang?

I wasn't too fond of the bosses overall, but I did like the [spoiler]Ra's al Ghul[/spoiler] fight and the [spoiler]Mr. Freeze[/spoiler] fight. Ironically the best part of the [spoiler]Ra's al Ghul[/spoiler] fight is actually when you're not fighting him, but a huge crowd of enemies, and it's a good test of your endurance and mastery of the game's fighting style. [spoiler]Mr. Freeze[/spoiler] is a stealth challenge, and might honestly be the best stealth-based boss fight in gaming history, putting you in a room filled with tactics you can use, but each time you the enemy adapts so you can't try the same trick twice.

And of course being able to play as Catwoman is fun. It's a bit ironic that I think Batman actually moves faster in combat (his ground takedown and counter animations feel faster), considering Catwoman is supposed to be the agile one, but overall her style is both unique enough and deep enough to be worth playing, although Batman has more options for both stealth and combat.

The story itself is peak Batman. I like that it's not just a mission to save innocent people, but also to save criminals from cruel and unusual punishment in this prison city, as it highlights that Batman is also about giving criminals a chance to reform (even if they never actually do). It is odd, though, that from the beginning the villain Hugo Strange knows that Batman is Bruce Wayne, but this has almost no importance to the story. I guess maybe Dr. Strange wants to be able to beat Batman without revealing his identity, but it just doesn't feel like Batman's identity being known is as big of an issue as it should be.

If I had any complaint, it's that there's too many Riddler challenges. When you're just progressing through the game they make a fun diversion, and it's nice that each challenge is a unique puzzle. But with so many, you're almost guaranteed to complete the game before you find them all, so you'll reach a point where Riddler challenges are the [i]only[/i] thing you're doing for a while. And Riddler's actual side quest requires you to complete these challenges to get access to his actual challenge rooms where you can save his hostages.

Regarding the quality of the PC version, the only issue I had is that somehow playing this game makes Windows think my Bluetooth headphones are speakers, and the first time I booted this game up Windows decided to crank my volume all the way up to 100 and destroy my eardrums.

Okay, jokes aside Batman Arkham City is probably one of the best Batman stories ever told. If you liked Arkham Asylum then you're going to love the sequel. Arkham City has a story so deep that it will make you realize why Batman is held in such high regard when it comes to comic book superheroes. The story picks up about a year after the first game. Without wasting any more time, I'll try to summarize everything you need to know.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
+Arkham City is absolutely stunning and beautifully crafted open world with lot of love and care. The city is divided into many small districts with distinctive colors and building structures. It’s about five times the size of Arkham Asylum.
+Features a large ensemble cast of characters. If you think your favorite Batman villains were absent in Arkham Asylum then chances are they're present in this game. The villains and supporting cast are equally well written as Batman. 
+Voice acting by Kevin Conroy and Mark Hamill brings a nostalgic life to Batman and Joker. Other voice actors also did an excellent job.
+The soundtrack is a masterpiece! The theme song fits so well into the Batman universe. Warner bros has also recorded an original score. 
+Combat is extremely simple yet addictive and satisfying at the same time. The game also features lots of predator encounters where you’re allowed to use stealth and take your enemies one by one without been seen. You should have a blast completing these predetor encounters. 
+The addictive free flow combat system from Arkham Asylum is better than ever with new tweaks to suit open world gameplay. Enemy A.I is now even smarter because the enemies will hit you and counter block your attacks if you keep button mashing. Gameplay is very well polished and optimized even for low-end PCs. Overall an excellent PC port.
+Well balanced gameplay. As you unlock new gadgets and abilities by progressing and levelling up Batman, the enemies also become smarter and more challenging. At first, they start using baseball bats and then they'll slowly use to broken shards, knives, shields, body armors and finally guard their boss’ territory with snipers. The guys who work at Rocksteady are really smart, aren’t they?
+There’s a good portion of the story exclusive for Catwoman but do not mistake her for a reskinned version of Batman because she has her own attack styles, arsenal of toys, she can crawl over walls, pounce on enemies and go to some places where even Batman cannot. 
+Great assortment of involving side missions makes terrific use of a host of Batman characters
+Arkham City makes best use easter eggs and references. Can’t think of any game that does it better! 
+Steam cloud saving, Steam achievements and trading cards.
+You get all the DLC extras that GFWL PC, PS3 and Xbox 360 customers would need to pay easily twice as much to obtain singularly in all-in-one bundle. Be sure to check out Harley Quinn’s Revenge story DLC after finishing the main game. The DLC can be launched through main menu. 

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-440 Riddler trophies and challenges should be overkill even for Batman. C’mon guys he is Gotham’s Dark Knight. The city needs him to solve crimes and defeat the evil and not jump from one puzzle to the next. You can’t give do this to Batman!
-WB Games didn't even care to bring Batman: Return to Arkham Remastered Collection on PC. Maybe it had something to do with Arkham Knight’s PC port?

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
This is the one game that I never get tired of playing. I’ve played this game for hundreds of hours both on PC and PS4 and I can see myself playing it again in the future. This game has an amazing opening and a truly spectacular and unbelievable ending. There is a reason why Batman Arkham City won several Game of The Year awards in 2011. There’s enough content to keep you busy for 30-40 hours. Don’t hesitate to buy Arkham City because it’s based on comic books. I’m sure you’ll love it if you’re looking for a good single player experience. I would Recommend getting the whole Arkham Trilogy on a sale.

Arkham City, that's where the party is at. It still is, by the way. Good game back in the day, good game today as well, a true classic I'd say. Haven't seen a list of top 10 best superhero or batman games where this doesn't take the first place. We all have our favorites, but this one is objectively good. Clever design, fluid and satisfying combat, rolling story that ends with a bang, collectibles that are fun to pick, challenges that are fun to complete, it's a real shame no dev has made this their bible, not even Rocksteady.

Without giving too much away, Arkham City is an area of Gotham were the criminal and mentally insane, all part of an initiative which gets Batman in the thick of it, as intended. Hugo Strange is the villain who's throwing the dice in taking the bat down, along with special forces and other schemes, yet the Joker shows up with something to keep Batman on the move. It's these two that weave the plot, yet there are plenty of side characters that take part in the main plot, such as Two Face, Penguin and Mr. Freeze, and others like Bane, Hush, Azrael, Deadshot and Zsazs in secondary missions. It all flows naturally, though I'll have to say, some secondary instances won't happen unless you do some free roaming.
The plot itself is engaging and leaves an impact at every step, some bigger than others, making it replayable just for the gist of it. 

The combat is what earned the series its renown and this is where I find it to shine the most in the whole franchise. You don't need complicated controls for combos, as special combos and quick fire gadgets happen at the press of one button. Frankly, the more you use in combat, the more you're going to enjoy it all. Gadgets can be unexpectedly useful outside their original design. While saying that you can experiment with them is a stretch, I'd say they are fun surprises. Crowd control, crowd finishers, special finishers, weapon disarming, all of those can be bought as upgrades and make Batman the Man in every fight, making every encounter a stylish beating of the poor bastards that think they can take down the living legend. The thing about combat is: the more you embrace its variety, the more you're going to enjoy it. What you can do in a fight ain't much to remember, but the level design will make you think quick at times. Predator instances require an use of the environment, gargoyles, gadgets and terrifying henchmen to the point where they'd consider lying down and pretending to be dead if the A.I. had that in its programming.

Upgrades are handled in probably the best way. Instead of going through chains to unlock the thing you want, you can get it directly. Simply select the improvement you want and bam, you have it. The two exceptions are the upgrades to armor, the ballistic and the combat side of it. 

The city is a hub filled with collectibles, riddles and a couple of secrets. There's the chatter of the henchmen which will amuse you or give you hints about several plot points. They will draw your attention, but won't make you lose focus on your objective, as they stand eclipsed by the story-lines. 

Visually the game looks great, DX11 tessellation being solved by modern hardware and physiX can make this game look next gen even today. Higher resolutions will make the game keep up and I'll say that I haven't noticed a low res texture in the game. 

A great bonus for the game is Riddler's Revenge, a set of challenges where you can play as Batman, Catwoman, Robin and Nightwing, challenges where you'll beat four waves of enemies and predator encounters. The four characters handle differently from each other, staying true to their style and warranting going through the challenges again. The point in those challenges is to reach a certain score in the fighting ones and to do specific actions in the predator ones. There are also campaigns which consist of sets of combined challenges.

You can play as Catwoman in the main campaign as well and free roam after it as well by using a switch point between her and Batman. She's not as fast in terms of exploration, but she's smooth and sexy, handles like a purring cat. Her outfit zip is down enough to draw attention and influence some people's dreams, but high enough to keep the rating PG-13. 

A thing I'll mention for those with high refreshing monitors: the game is capped at 62 fps, typical for Unreal Engine 3 games. On the other hand, Gsync will make a difference. For me, the combat and gliding are even more of a joy because of it. 

It's one of the the games I can recommend to anyone at full price. You know it's a good game when you feel like saying "They don't make them like this anymore!"

The combat is unsatisfying. It can be fun here and there, but there just isn’t any depth. It doesn’t feel earned. I didn’t come away from it feeling like Batman. I felt like I was just playing a very violent rhythm game. On top of that, it’s weird in practice, too. Sometimes Batman will leap across two screens to attack a bad guy, then he’ll fumble an attack on a bad guy right next to him. There’s no rhyme or logic to it. And you’ll be pissed off when it happens because you then lose your combo for no good reason.

The game is utterly filled with content, but that doesn’t mean it is good content. It is Filler City. It is seriously padded out with a lot of meaningless content that is either trifling at best or just atrocious at worst. It suffers all the pitfalls of a Ubisoft-style open-world and is no more compelling for it. The side activities are shoddily implemented and feel tacked on as a way to expose the player to more of Batman’s rogues gallery. Unfortunately, it just doesn’t work for creating a fun or interesting experience. Why would I care to see more of these characters when the experience is the same for every one of them? They aren’t interesting to see. They are window dressing. I feel like 75-85% of the game could have easily been cut. And the resources dedicated to more meaningful, interesting content. 


The story is just abysmal. Batman himself is completely uninteresting here and the central dilemma plaguing him and the world at large is equally uncompelling. He has zero personality beyond delivering gruff lines to everyone around him while all the characters you interact with are homicidal maniacs that would be better off dead. The villains are particularly heinous here and it beggars belief that Batman lets them live after the crap they pull off repeatedly in the game. Even the villains that aren’t wholly evil act idiotic here, too, and it drags the story down even further.

There are two massive drivers of events in the game and one is completely shrouded in mystery til the very end, so you have zero reason to care about it. And the other is much more immediate, but due to the flat performances and needlessly tacked on filler, it doesn’t feel urgent at all. It is barely a blip in your mind. And you feel there are no stakes whatsoever to what you are doing.

I know Batman is a gruff character with a somber demeanor, but he’s more than that. We have seen him across a large variety of media. And he can be so much more. And be more dynamic and interesting. He’s complex with a lot of issues that extend well beyond the surface. And we just don’t see any of that here. It’s just the most surface-level interpretation of Batman being Batman and that’s that. 

I came away from this game feeling like I may have enjoyed parts of it, but it was ultimately just a tedious experience and after playing other games, my opinion has been revised downwards. It just isn’t a good game. It wasn’t even a good game for its time. I’ve played a ton of games from its time period recently and it doesn’t measure up to any of them. I know my opinion is in the minority, but hey, it is what it is.

Batman Arkham City is my favorite game of all time. It has some major talent and passion behind it only releasing two years after Arkham Asylum, it’s a beautiful game that warrants a playthrough from anyone. So let's step into the shoes of Batman and Talk about it. (Play the total paranoia intro) 

Arkham City released October 18th 2011 for Xbox 360,PS3, and Pc. With development for the game starting before Asylum was even complete, which is crazy. That just shows their confidence in Asylum. Arkham City easily makes me feel like Batman most of the time because I feel like I’m in Gotham and not parts of big American cities. 

The map is one of this game's strong points and I haven’t seen a game map littered with so much life since. Only in Gotham and I’m gonna see a chemical plant next to a movie theater, only in gotham and I gonna see a sign that says live nudes next to a courthouse. It has streets barely narrow for cars meant for what seems like pedestrians. It shows age, there are billboards and businesses referencing characters who are not in a single Arkham game, like Rat Catcher, Maxie Zeus, and Sal Maroni. The entire courthouse is burnt in half a reflection of Two-Face and his sense of duality. Every building and every street has some story to tell, small or not. Arkham City is so full of life with architecture that clash together such as the Steel Mill and the Monarch Theater yet they feel like they are in the same world perfectly. And I love the Fact you can see Arkham Island from the GCPD and you can see that the plants and the events have affected the Island. The Collapsed Streets are eerie and you can tell they are from a withering. Gotham is a reflection of Batman and The Jokers during this game, decaying, weary,fading. And the immersion with the map is so alive with  the thug dialogue and assaults on political prisoners. I look at Arkham City and I see a place that was once a metropolis where the wealthy would prosper and the honest, but now it’s become corrupt and taken by greed.The steel mill feels like a maze with twists and turns that open up littered with balloons, and clowns galore. The museum feels like a fortress with trophies and monuments to why Gotham should fear the Penguin. The GCPD is bitter, and a reflection of how the cops have failed to keep the city safe. With the inside being repurposed to a lab with the single purpose of curing Mr.Freeze’s wife Nora. with Wonder Tower towering over the entire prison where Hugo Strange can just watch and learn. 

Arkham City is a story about death. In some way every main character that shows up is a reflection of that with Batman and Joker slowly dying. Two-Face may as well be half dead. Ra’s Al Ghul constant;y cheating death. Hugo Strange plans on killing everyone within this concrete hell. Mr.Freeze is a man trying to save his dying wife.Strange put up a light and an audio tape at the memorial of Thomas and Martha Wayne to pretty mock Bruce, just to show how death affects someone. Even though most of the story is a wild goose chase some would say, I would say it’s some of Paul Dini’s best work with Batman. It’s as good as stuff like Heart of Ice and Mad Love. Unlike Arkham Asylum it’s not just a simple comic esc adventure. Arkham City is a much Darker Gritty story. And believe me Arkham Asylum is pretty dark but as much as City. Arkham City isn’t as black and white as Asylum, some characters act as allies but can’t fully be trusted such as Mr.Freeze or Tailia Al Ghul. Arkham City shows the consequences of actions in Asylum also. With Penguin having titan, and Joker dying due to an overdose of that same drug. Hugo Strange and Quincy Sharp opened up Arkham city not only because of Ra’s grand plan but also because of the Arkham Island Riots. The game opens with a painting depicting Cane carrying the body of Able, the first murder in the bible, and Arkham City closes with Batman carrying Joker's corpse. It ends and begins with death.

 A sequel should always improve on the original, and that’s exactly what Arkham City did gameplay wise. Rocksteady looked at what worked and refined it, the traversal improved with being able to dive bomb while gliding and adding the Grapnel boost which is a must have on every playthrough. You pretty much start with every skill and gadget that you ended with in Asylum, Including the beautiful batclaw and inverted takedown. A new array of gadgets to have fun and utilize in your play through too. Don’t get me started on the Combat it’s just perfection, truly addicting and so just fluid and brutal. Feels and looks like something I would Batman do in the comics. The predator sections are so much more fun with new tactics and challenges that make you get more creative with each encounter. The boss fights while not the best in the series are definitely up there. The Mr.Freeze fight is easily one the greatest boss fights of all time, making you do a different takedown each time shows how smart he is with how Freeze adapts. The introduction of the mine enemies and body armor thugs are a fun challenge. Arkham City did a wonderful job on improving what Asylum did right.

Arkham City also has some of the best character designs. Batman’s suit is the best take on a comic accurate suit of all time. Mr.Freeze looks sick as hell. Joker is just as lanky as he needs to be. Batman is also huge like he should be. His forearm alone is like the size of Harley Quinn. Two-Face looks awesome with his burned self. Arkham City looks like a moving comic.

All in all Batman Arkham CIty is a wonderful game, that’s an experience. An experience child me watched my dad playthrough only to finally play through it myself pretty much a decade later. I’ve played the game four times in the last two years. I believe and will stand by Arkham CIty being something everyone should play through at least once. It has so much passion and love behind it. It’s a piece of media that has and will continue to be a great introduction into the amazing world of Batman to many people.

Arkham City is a brilliant game, just like the other games in the series (even Origins to some extent) but it's also just as frustrating sometimes.

I don't know whose decision was it to include those Riddler informants in almost every combat encounter, including the ones in campaign missions but I hated how a side mission/activity bled into the main story like that. The whole signature free flow combat sytem of the game favours and revolves around getting a higher combo but because of those informants at every turn you have to be "careful" when beating up thugs as you need to leave the informant for last. I know it's optional to deal with them and I didn't even bother to do all of the Riddler stuff anyways but after finishing the game I have maybe more than five combat encounters that left me satisfied. I wish it was the same deal with Origins, where informants are usually on their lonesome in the wild and the challenge is to simply find them all rather than having to deal with them even when you don't want to. Riddler's overall side missions are fine on their own (didn't bother to complete them all either unfortunately) and almost the entirety of the puzzles I cared to get through were great, yet the informants and the sheer amount of other challenges you are expected to complete (around two to three hundred just to be done with the initial string of missions if my memory serves me right) to get to him just wasn't all that appealing to me.

Then--and I believe it'll be a highly unpopular opinion--the narrative felt way too convoluted. I do love how the entire game kinda felt like a long, long episode of BtAS (which I love) but with the amount of villains that get introduced and effect the story became a little too much for my taste after a certain point. Almost none of them get the screen time they need to meaningfully establish themselves in the overall story and the worst of all the "main" villain was just a tad bit too... Passive, I guess, to truly make me feel like they were a threat I needed to take down. To give writers some credit, there were many moments that prevented me from just putting the controller down, I needed to see where the story was going to take me and it does have quite an impactful ending as well with intricate and clever details hinting at the that final resolution yet I just think the story loses its focus often and stretches itself far too thin. Many of the missions and characters can merit their own game if you'd tried hard enough or even maybe combined a couple of them together. However, too much is indeed too much sometimes.

Talking about convoluted, I also have to say I didn't enjoy how [i]City[/i] just throws everyting at you the moment you start the game. On one hand, there is just so much to do in Arkham City; with numerous side missions, activities, challenges and just stuff to find and to an extent simple events to behold, you are never a moment bored or feel aimless. On the other hand however, everything happens at the same time which can feel overwhelming at times. Just by going from one mission to another you can encounter several of those activities and those just don't wait for you either. You actively have to intervene most of them and if you don't feel up to it at the time and would rather do them at your next convenience, tough luck, you simply can't as they just get triggered at random intervals as you make your way throughout the game which to be fair, is highly immersive and very on-brand with Batman mythos but I felt it was too much for me. Maybe it's just my inexperience with open world games but I gotta say I felt a lot less "attacked by" with Asylum or even with Origins rather than with City. Can be completely personal.

Finally, to be done with the negatives, I have to mention the performance issues. Even though the game runs fine on stable 62 fps (for some reason) most of the time, I often encountered sudden dips mainly before and after cutscenes and sometimes even roaming around in the open world. I think this is a mixture of the game getting significantly old which can explain certain issues whilst running on modern systems and this particular port being not of best quality, even for its time. I'd like to say this was all that there was but at certain moments during [spoiler]Clayface[/spoiler] boss fight, right after he [spoiler]hits a wall and explodes[/spoiler], I was suddenly watching a slideshow, and it wasn't a short time one either as I had to wait a solid half-minute for it to stop. The thing is, it wasn't a one time occurance since the particular moment I mentioned happens a couple times during the boss fight and every time it did, I was having the same issue. To the point I thought some [i]Asylum[/i]-esque fourth-wall-breaking shenanings were happening. In short, you can take this as your final warning to finally play City since you might be dependent on some community patches to run it with your top-of-the-line system in the near future.

At this point, right before I get into why I really like [i]City[/i] after going through every single issue I went through mentioned up above, I have to confess that I had extremely high expectations from it. This was supposed to be the absolute best Arkham game after all, this was the game that Rocksteady ironed out every tiny inconvenience there was in [i]Asylum[/i] to finally come up with a masterpiece of a game and to a point it actually is. Every single voice actor showed up for their character even for minor mobs all over in the game's world, overall art design is simply perfect and when combined with the still decent graphics the game just refuses to age and I can confidently say between Asylum, Origins and Knight I enjoyed City's combat the most, free flow combat system at its core is simply one of the most enjoyable combat systems in the entire gaming industry anyways or hell just being Batman with all the cool gadgets he has never gets old and is an absolute treat. Even a couple aspects I listed on their own can create a worthwhile game and [i]City[/i] just has all of them combined. So yeah, even with with all the minor issues holding it back I think it's a good if not a great game. Then why this review, why I couldn't have just typed "Great game, recommended." and called it a day?

Well I tried. I tried to love City, tried to thoroughly enjoy it. But one Riddler informant at a time or just me getting overly stimulated with everything being thrown at my face or just slightly struggling with traversal (I just think without every upgrade, it can be annoying honestly) or maybe finding some of the places the story took me feeling a little unnecessary, I simply couldn't. Moments I purely enjoyed were almost only limited to combat challenges where I could finally beat the everliving sh*t out of some goons without having to deal with some green-glowing son of a b*tch getting in my way as one of the coolest superheroes ever created. Pure bliss. To the point that I can go and say those combat challenges were the reason why there is a blue thumbs up above this mess of a review.

At the end of the day, I don't know what to blame. My shoddy taste? Expectations? Asylum being my first in the Arkham series and holding a special place in my heart? Not sure, and none of those make City any less great. I just... Couldn't love it despite all my hopes. Still recommend it though. Definitely play it as soon as you can before it becomes unplayable without mods or community patches.

Moving from Arkham Asylum to Arkham City feels smooth yet sudden. 
Asylum was claustrophobic, tightly designed and focused. A singleplayer corridor experience where every room felt handcrafted
City opens the gates at the end of those claustrophic corridors from Asylum. 
The world expands, the atmosphere shifts and suddenly you're not infiltrating an insane facility but instead you're patrolling a living decaying part of Gotham.

If Asylum felt like the perfect Batman simulator then City takes that formula and elevates it. Few games capture the fantasy of being Batman as well as stalking on a rooftop, listening to cries for help echo through the streets and deciding where to intervene next. The sense of presence is extraordinary.

+ Arkham City starts strong and ends strong. The area itself is a spectacular environment to explore filled with atmosphere. Even though the map is broader and more open than Asylum, that oppressive, suffocating tone never disappears. It's still dark, cold and hostile. 
+ Villains lurk around every corner and the constant pressure of the city's madness weighs on Batman throughout the story. 
+ The story expands to include more villains while still following the consequences of Asylum, with Joker's actions still affecting everything.
+ Combat is deeper and more varied with new gadgets and enemy types. The city is packed with side missions and secrets. 
+ The thug radio chatter adds a surprising amount of world‑building. Some quests are creepy and the game's atmosphere remains unmatched in the genre.

- On the negative side...Catwoman's inclusion is a great addition, though her role feels underused. She opens the game with a bang but then disappears for most of the story and returns only near the end as if the game suddenly remembered she existed. Still, her segments add great variety and she feels wonderful to use.
You do get the option to play as her freely after you beat the game so that's pretty awesome.

If you loved Arkham Asylum, Arkham City is a natural evolution which is pretty rare for a sequel...It's bigger, richer, more ambitious, and still visually impressive today. It's a world worth getting lost in so don't sleep on it even if you're not a big batman fan.

Batman Arkham City is the perfect sequel. It improves on virtually every aspect of its already fantastic predecessor, combat, detective work and riddles. It gives you an open world in which you can glide around to your hearts content, solving side cases, each of which are incredible little crime stories of their own, and a main Batman story that is much darker and more gritty than anything we have previously experienced and honestly really well written, one of the best Batman stories there are to be honest, with actual consequences and characters dying, pushing the Detective to his mental and physical limits. The characters are also quite honestly the best version of themselves here, Catwoman, Mr.Freeze, Hugo Strange, Zasz, the Joker, they all feel so grounded somehow while still being fantastical in an almost mythic way, and for me at least, the Arkham games are my favorite version of Batman and his world, violent, gritty and noir, authentically Batman. Arkham City achieves all this without sacrificing any of the atmosphere or vibe that made Asylum so great, so yes, Arkham City is the perfect sequel, and in my and many others opinion deserves a spot on the Greatest Games of All Time List. I really cannot sing its praises enough, and you should play it as soon as you can, with the Arkham City Redux if you want completely remastered textures, even though the gothic art design holds up more than well enough, offering us perhaps the definitive version of Gotham.

Perhaps a few years ago, few people thought that Batman, the beloved black knight who had long since risen from the top and was no longer a name in the world of games and cinema, would suddenly once again conquer the peaks of success one after another. get new fans as well. The success of the cinema also made its way into the gaming world, and Arkham Asylum was so great that it was named the best superhero game in the history of computer games at the time of its release. Now we can confidently tell you that Batman: Arkham City has not only overtaken Arkham Asylum and immortalized Batman's name forever.

The one-on-one battles formed the basis of the game in the previous issue, a fascinating and breathtaking battle that deepened Batman's gameplay with a variety of techniques performed by Batman. This issue also uses the same successful formula of the previous game and by improving the problems of that title, it puts itself at the top of the table of the hand-to-hand fights of this generation! Arkham City is full of dangerous criminals and criminals scattered throughout the city, with the sole purpose of destroying Batman. The number of enemies in this game is more than the previous number, and due to the large area of the map, in some places, countless enemies will fight you. The key to success in combat is the correct use of attack and counter-attack and the correct understanding of the enemy's position. At first glance, you might think that by pressing the key to attacking easily, you can easily defeat the enemies of the game, but rest assured that this will only cause Batman to die early! Each enemy has its own method of attack, the common enemies that use punches and kicks to attack you, or the enemies that greet you with knives or electric shocks. As we progress in the game, the number of enemies and their diversity has increased, and in order to win the battles, we must act in a well-planned manner. To eliminate any enemy, you must use special techniques, and for example, the method of destroying the enemy that has a shield in hand is completely different from the ninja who attacks you with a sword. In the final stages, the enemies attack you in different ways and at the same time, in which case you must destroy the enemies in order of priority. This special method of fighting makes not only the fights not to be boring until the end of the game, but always make you thirst for fights. The game's struggles, in addition to being very deep and calculated, have an indescribable charm. During the game, you will feel the weight of all the blows that Batman inflicts on the enemies, especially the final finishers of each fight, which is depicted as a slow and beautiful image, which makes you who winning a breathtaking fight, very happy!

As with the previous game, the stealth part is one of the main parts of the game. In this section, you must confront the armed enemies with firearms and secretly destroy them with the help of statues hanging from the ceiling, air conditioning ducts, or ducts located on the ground. enemies with the strong weapon in their hands, the idea of fighting them hand in hand is often wrong! This part of the game has improved a lot compared to the previous game, and the artificial intelligence of the enemies in this one is higher and they react to the slightest incident in the environment, especially in the final stages. One or two shots will kill you, so the only way to destroy them is to use the game environment properly and follow the principles of stealth. The best way to get rid of these enemies is to hang a statue, in which case you can replace the enemy that passes under the statue whit your self! The only downside to hiding is that sometimes enemies gather at a point where you can confuse them with a smoke grenade and then easily knock'em out. Combining hand-to-hand combat and stealth, and the proper arrangement of these stages throughout the game creates great and almost flawless gameplay that will amaze any player.


In this game, the world's greatest detective uses a complete set of equipment and devices for scanning the environment. In addition to the items in the previous game, there is new equipment in this section, including items you can get from Mr. Freeze. For example, one of these items creates an ice mold on the water that is necessary to use in one of the stages of the game, so all your equipment, is used during the game and none of them have the role of appearance and filling screen! The Detective Mode feature in this version also plays an essential role in the game, and in addition to the puzzle section, it will also be widely used in the combat section. With the help of this feature, all the sensitive parts of the environment as well as the enemies of the game are highlighted and information from these parts is provided to you, which is a vital solution for advancing the puzzle part of the game. Hacking security locks is one of the things that happens a lot during the game, but unfortunately, the game hacking system is very easy and trivial, and you can easily unlock a high-security lock in 4 or 5 seconds. The mini-game designed for this section has a simple design and its difficulty level does not change much during the game, which in this respect has fallen behind the previous version. The enigmatic part and its breadth prevent the game from getting boring and give a good variety to the gameplay.


Arkham City art design is very beautiful and artistic and will surprise you in some parts. Due to the fact that most of the stages of the game take place during the night, the special lighting of the game, and the appearance of the lights in different parts of the environment, the feeling of darkness and horror in the city inspires you well. Also, although most of the time the game is played in dark spaces, the game environments will not be repeated in any way. The quality of the textures of the environment is acceptable due to the wide range of the game and the faces of the characters have a unique design. The animation of Batman and Enemies is one of the positive points of the game, and the movement of Batman's cape during the flight and his change of direction has been excellent. The view of the game environment is so beautiful that in some parts you inadvertently fall on a tall building and stare at the horrible view under your feet for a few minutes! The details used in the game environment are so great that you will see a subtle and interesting point in each place.

The voice acting of the game's characters is of high quality, and the voice actors still do their job well. Kevin Conroy as Batman and Mark Hamill as the Joker have given special beauty to the game's sound acting, while Nolan North has elevated this part's value by playing the role of penguin. The sound effects of the environment, such as the breaking of objects and the sound of enemies and their arrogance, all have a good design. The game's music is very audible and makes the dark atmosphere of the game very believable. The rhythm of the music played during the fights is in good harmony with the atmosphere of the game, and next to them, the epic theme that can be heard in some parts will make you get goosebumps.

Batman: Arkham City is no ordinary game, a title that will stay in your memory for a long time and is easily one of the best games of the last few years. The high quality of the game is evident in all its parts and shows the seriousness of Rocksteady to make a game worthy of admiration. The game's progress is much higher than before, and the gameplay is so engaging and breathtaking that it will never be repeated for you.
